skills.name: The Great Depression: boom, crash and deepening contraction

note.text: The US economy expanded during the 1920s, but prosperity was uneven and speculative borrowing increased vulnerability. The downturn began in 1929; the October stock-market crash damaged wealth and confidence. Later banking panics and contracting credit deepened the collapse. Weak demand, deflation and international financial links helped spread difficulties. The crash was important but not a complete single-cause explanation. A financial event, the mechanism amplifying it and the wider depression should be distinguished.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish boom vulnerabilities, the stock-market crash and banking amplification. Builds on: industrial production, markets and unequal gains. Leads to: manifestations and international consequences of the Depression.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: The US economy expanded during the {1920}s, but prosperity was uneven and speculative borrowing increased vulnerability. The downturn began in {1929}; the October stock-market crash damaged wealth and confidence. Later banking panics and contracting credit deepened the collapse. Weak demand, deflation and international financial links helped spread difficulties. The crash was important but not a complete single-cause explanation. A financial event, the mechanism amplifying it and the wider depression should be distinguished.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: US banking panics developed during {1930}–{1931}; the national banking emergency reached a critical point in March {1933}. A factory’s falling orders, depositors’ withdrawals and reduced credit could reinforce one another. The order matters: later tariff restrictions or policy decisions cannot simply be presented as events that occurred before the {1929} crash.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: Speculative borrowing increased exposure to a fall in share prices.
Selling and falling prices damaged confidence and wealth.
Banking panics disrupted credit and payments after the crash.
Reduced lending and trade connected the downturn to other countries.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Every household benefited equally and no vulnerability existed during the boom. Correction: Growth can coexist with unequal gains and risk.
The crash alone explains every feature of a decade-long global depression. Correction: Banking, demand, policy and international mechanisms also mattered.
All banking panics in this account occurred only before the {1929} crash. Correction: The {1930}–{1931} panics followed it.
Every economy was isolated from international finance and trade. Correction: Cross-border relationships helped transmit shocks.
